environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 2000 m (6562 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; 5 to 93 percent short term
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) normal operation

features.expansion: two bays, QFX-EM-4Q (4 x 40 GbE QSFP+) and EX4600-EM-8F (8 x 10 GbE SFP+), 32 QSFP+ ports at most
features.optics-qsfp: 40 GbE QSFP+, QSFP+ direct attach and active optical cable, breakout cables to SFP+
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches in a ring; also a Virtual Chassis Fabric spine or leaf and a QFabric node or interconnect

management.oob: management port C0 (RJ-45, em0) and C1 (SFP, em1) with link and status lamps
management.usb: one USB port for image updates

performance.qsfp-plus-speeds: 40 GbE; or four 10 GbE with a breakout cable

physical.weight-note: 22 lb (9.97 kg per the guide, 21.6 lb or 9.8 kg per the datasheet) with FRUs installed (Table 3)

power.power-input-ac: 110 to 240 VAC single phase (datasheet); the guide's table gives no value
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 to -72 VDC, 10 A maximum (guide Table 17)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing and fully redundant; both should be installed

thermal.fans: five fan modules, hot-swappable; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

gaps.wanted: The datasheet prints 161 W for the QFX5100-24Q-AFO/AFI under "Power Consumption", the guide 230 W typical and 365 W maximum (Table 14). Same device, no measure or scope stated for the 161 W. The guide's figures are carried.
The guide's Table 3 gives 22 lb (9.97 kg) with FRUs, the datasheet 21.6 lb (9.8 kg). The guide's is carried.
The datasheet gives -36 to -72 V DC; the guide's Table 17 gives -40 through -72 VDC (rated -48 to -60). The guide's range is carried.
The guide's Table 14 prints no value for AC input voltage, line frequency or current in the PDF held. The datasheet gives 110-240 V single phase.
The part number of the four-post mounting kit, and its depth ranges. The guide describes the kit and flush or recessed mounting in prose and a figure per chassis but gives no part number.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port "for image updates" and gives no generation. It is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The vertical rating label at the right edge of the rear is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.
The yellow laser hazard label at the lower right of the last port group. It is a label, not a feature of the metal, and is reserved as a region.

The photograph shows no fan numerals, fan icons or supply symbols on the strips beside the slots. The guide numbers the fan slots 0 to 4 and its figure draws the marks. They are not drawn on this device.

A photograph or flat drawing of the three-port management panel on a 24Q. The guide's Figure 22 draws it without scale, and the only photograph of it is the 48T's. The rear-3mgmt view takes the 48S's arrangement.

Reseller trackers list end-of-life announcements of 2020 to 2022 for the QFX5100-24Q part numbers. The guide and the datasheet (July 2024) state none and the Juniper bulletin was not reached, so none is recorded.

Whether the 24 fixed ports carry printed numerals. The photograph shows none beside their lamps while the module ports' numerals resolve in it; no larger image is held, and the guide's drawing is a thumbnail.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

chassis.note: guide Table 3: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52 cm) deep, 22 lb (9.97 kg) with FRUs installed. The datasheet gives 4.37 x 44.09 x 52.02 cm, the same size, and 21.6 lb (9.8 kg). The two weights disagree by 0.4 lb and the guide's is carried. The width is the body: the mounting brackets are not part of it and are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate around the ports samples #55585f (a 8 by 4 px mean between two lamps) and the rear panel #6c7076. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference. The front is carried.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide says the switch mounts flush or recessed 2 in (5 cm) in a four-post rack with the mounting kit shipped with it (a pair of front rails and two rear blades; twelve screws), and gives no part number for the kit; the datasheet says only "versatile four post mounting options". The library holds no kit contract for it, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

esd.note: Guide Figure 11 callout 1, the electrostatic discharge terminal, is the round jack at the lower left, centred 6.4 mm across and 38.8 mm down in the photograph, with the ESD mark drawn above it in the figure.

gate-1.note: The front studio photograph is orthographic enough to measure. Its body runs from column 21 to 1465, 1445 px, and from row 41 to 184.5, 143.5 px, an aspect of 10.07 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09, 0.2 percent out. Scale 3.277 px/mm across and 3.284 down. The rear photograph reads 1440 x 143 px (columns 34 to 1473, rows 29.5 to 172.7), 10.07, 0.2 percent out, at 3.266 px/mm across. Every position read off them is good to a pixel, 0.3 mm, and is estimated.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. The guide and the datasheet (July 2024) state none. Reseller trackers list announcements of 2020 to 2022 for the QFX5100-24Q part numbers, which the maker's documents do not repeat, so the device states none announced and a gap records the trackers' claim. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

mgmt.note: Table 1: the AFO, AFI and DC-AFO and DC-AFI models have two management ports, the 3AFO, 3AFI, D-3AFO and D-3AFI models three. The photograph shows the two-port panel: C1 is the SFP cage (em1) and C0 the lower of the two stacked RJ-45 jacks (em0); the upper jack is the console. The guide's Figure 22 also draws a three-port panel (a second SFP cage, C0, above C1), which is the `rear-3mgmt` view. Its arrangement is the 48S's, taken from the QFX5100-48T photograph, because no 24Q photograph of it is held.

modules.note: The two bays at the right of the port panel (guide Figure 11 callout 3, "Expansion module bays with cover panels (2)"). The photograph shows a QFX-EM-4Q in each, whose faces start at 261 mm, with the seam at 348.5 mm. The two bays are the EX4600's, 86.7 x 43.2 mm at 262.4 and 349.1 mm, of the same module (the QFX-EM-4Q and the blank are the same parts as the EX4600's, and the guide's Figures 6 and 7 are the same modules) and the same size; the library's modules for them are reused. The guide numbers no bay, so they are em-0 and em-1 from the left. The guide says the switch is "configured for the QFX-EM-4Q by default" and the datasheet lists the QFX5100-EM-BLNK blank module, so the shipped state is the cover panel and the modules are ordered separately. The QFX5100-24Q-AA, whose bay takes the double-wide QFX-PFA-4Q, is a different front panel and is not modelled here.

modules-fru.note: The fan modules (QFX5100-FAN-AFO and -AFI) and the 650 W power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO, -AFI, and the DC -AFO and -AFI named by the datasheet) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component, reused from the QFX5100-48S by part number. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. The guide says to fit a blank cover over an empty supply slot but names no part number for it, so no blank is modelled for the supply slots.

port-lamps.note: Four dots stand above every upper cage and below every lower one, at 4.15 mm pitch, the second dot under the cage centre (guide Figure 12: the first lamp 10G/40G and the other three 10G; Table 4). The photograph resolves all 96 of them.

port-numbering.note: The ports are 0 to 23 (guide Figure 11 callout 2 and the text, "ports 0 through 23"). The photograph prints no numeral beside the lamps of the 24 fixed ports, though the numerals of the module ports (0 and 2 above, 1 and 3 below) resolve in the same photograph, which is the control, so nothing is printed for the fixed ports and no numeral is drawn. The guide's Figure 12 draws a numeral 48 at the left of the lamps, but it is the figure of the 48S's uplink port and not of this panel. The order of the ports is not given by the guide; they run down each column, 0 above 1 and 2 above 3, as the modules' ports do. Interface names are not printed on the unit and the guide's examples give none for the QSFP+ ports, so none is written.

ports.note: Front photograph. The 24 cages stand in four groups of three columns and two rows. The centres of the upper cages of column 0 to 11 read 76, 140, 202; 285, 347.5, 412.5; 495, 558, 620.5; 703, 766 and 829 px, a pitch of 63.1 px inside a group (19.25 mm, scale 3.277) and a group stride of 209.0 px (63.78 mm), so the gutter is 63.78 - 3 x 19.25 = 6.0 mm. The first cage centre is 16.78 mm from the left edge, so the 18.5 mm cells start at 7.53 mm. The registry's pitch for a ganged QSFP+ block is 19.0 mm; these are separate cages on a slightly wider pitch, so the photograph's 19.25 is used. Count is 24, callout 2 of figure 11.

power.note: guide Table 14 (AC): typical 230 W, maximum 365 W for the 24Q; Table 17 (DC): typical 300 W and maximum 385 W for the 24Q, 48S and 48T. The datasheet's "Power Consumption" prints 161 W for the 24Q-AFO/AFI without a measure or a scope. 161 W is below the guide's typical 230 W, so the two disagree and are recorded as a gap, not reconciled. The guide's figures are filed as the device's.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph, read at 4.5 times and compared with the QFX5100-48S's: the management panel (four chassis lamps, the C1 SFP cage with two lamps above it, the console and C0 jacks stacked in one shield, the USB port, the reset pinhole), five fan slots whose first edge is at 71.6 mm and whose pitch is 48.95 mm, two supply slots, and at the right edge the rating strip. Every position agrees with the 48S's to 0.5 mm (the lamps 0.45 mm, the C1 cage 0.5 mm, the USB port 0.4 mm), so the 48S's measured positions are used and the rear is the same panel. The photograph is of the back-to-front build.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The rear studio photograph is the back-to-front (AFI) build, with blue fan handles lettered AIR IN (AFI) and blue supply handles lettered AFI. The default configuration here is front-to-back (AFO) with Juniper Gold handles per Tables 13 and 19; the AFI configuration matches the photograph. The photograph's chip reads QFX5100-24Q and RUNNING JUNOS.

row-pitch.note: The cage faces of column 0 run from row 70.5 to 112 and from 117.5 to 158, centres 15.3 mm and 29.5 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 14.2 mm. The EX4600's QSFP+ cages, drawn from its own photograph, are 14.3 mm apart. The registry's 15.0 mm is not a conformance figure.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5100 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2023-02-26, 254 pages (Juniper Networks; terms: the guide's own copyright notice and the Juniper EULA, a reference copy kept outside the repository): Table 1 (models), Table 3 (physical specifications), Figure 5 and Figures 6 and 7 (the switch and its two expansion modules), Figure 11 and Table 4 (the port panel and its lamps), Figures 22 and 24 and 25 (management panel and lamps), Tables 12 to 14 and 17 (lamps, AC and DC supplies), Tables 19 to 21 (fan modules). QFX5100 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000480-022-EN, July 2024: the ordering table (variants, the expansion modules and the blank), weight, dimensions, power and the interface options. Juniper's studio photographs of the QFX5100-24Q, front and rear, 1500 x 251 and 1500 x 215 px (image library, qfx5100-24q-front-high and qfx5100-24q-rear-high), taken with a QFX-EM-4Q in each bay and the back-to-front build. The held intake folders for the Juniper EX, QFX and MX lines were searched (COVERAGE.md, SOURCES.md and INVENTORY.md of exqfx and mx, and the Visio and photo folders): none holds a Visio stencil or 3D model of a QFX5100, so every position is read off the photographs and the guide's flat figures. The guide's pictures are thumbnails and no drawing is copied.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the latch tongue at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention.

stickers.note: The yellow laser hazard label at the lower right of the last port group, 8 x 7.6 mm centred 253.6 across and 37.8 down, is an applied label and is reserved as a region, not drawn.

vents.note: Two staggered rows of hexagonal holes along the top edge (0.4 to 4.8 mm) and one band along the bottom (39.8 to 43.7 mm), from the left end of the ports to the expansion bays. They are drawn as vent strips with the hexagon pitch of the 48S (4.4 mm along the strip), an estimate.
